artists.biography:
The Rolling Stones are an English rock band formed in London in 1962. The first settled line-up consisted of Brian Jones on guitar and harmonica, Ian Stewart on piano, Mick Jagger on lead vocals and harmonica, Keith Richards on guitar and backing vocals, Bill Wyman on bass and Charlie Watts on drums. Jones founded and led the band, but Jagger and Richards assumed leadership after becoming the primary songwriters. Jones' increasing physical and mental troubles forced his departure from the band two weeks prior to his drowning death in 1969. Since Wyman retired in 1993, full band members have been Jagger, Richards, Watts and guitarist Ronnie Wood who joined in 1975, replacing Mick Taylor (who had followed Jones). The Rock and Roll Hall of Fame inducted the Rolling Stones in 1989. Rolling Stone magazine ranked them fourth on the "100 Greatest Artists of All Time" list and their album sales are estimated at more than 200 million worldwide.

The Rolling Stones were in the vanguard of the "British Invasion" of English bands that became popular in the U.S. in the mid-sixties. They have released twenty-four studio albums, eleven live albums and numerous compilations. Their album Sticky Fingers (1971) began a string of eight consecutive studio albums reaching number one in the United States. Their most recent album of new material, A Bigger Bang, was released in 2005. In 2008, Billboard magazine ranked the Rolling Stones at number ten on "The Billboard Top All-Time Artists" and as the second most successful group in the Billboard Hot 100 chart.

The Rolling Stones' advent brought greater international recognition to the primitive urban blues typified by Chess Records' artist Muddy Waters, writer of "Rollin' Stone", the song for which the band is named. Critic and musicologist Robert Palmer said their endurance and relevance stems from being "rooted in traditional verities, in rhythm-and-blues and soul music" while "more ephemeral pop fashions have come and gone". In 2012 the band celebrated their 50th anniversary.

apple_music.editorial_notes: Gathering up a variety of wild and bluesy rockers from the UK releases Out of Our Heads and Got Live If You Want It!, plus a handful of outtakes and singles, this 1965 set is like a musical junk drawer packed with unexpected treasure. Whether you're seeking the truculent stomp of “Get Off of My Cloud”, the orchestral-pop balladry of “As Tears Go By” or a fierce live rendition of “I’m Moving On”, this is an assortment to treasure year-round.
apple_music.name: December's Children (And Everybody's)

editorialNotes.short: A thrilling hodgepodge of rootsy outtakes from the pre-'66 Stones.

lastfm.wiki_content: "December's Children (And Everybody's)" is the fifth American studio album by the English rock band the Rolling Stones, released in December 1965. The album is primarily a compilation of tracks recorded across the band's career up to that point, including songs from the UK edition of "Out of Our Heads". Bassist Bill Wyman cites Mick Jagger in 1968 describing the record as " an album, it's just a collection of songs". The album includes the transatlantic hit single "Get Off of My Cloud" and a Rolling Stones remake of Marianne Faithfull's Jagger/Richards-written hit "As Tears Go By", which was issued as the album's second single in the United States. "December's Children (And Everybody's)" is the last of the group's early releases to feature a substantial number of cover songs, with Jagger and Keith Richards having written approximately half of the tracks. The album was not recorded in a dedicated session; many songs originate from the UK edition of "Out of Our Heads", recorded in September 1965 in Los Angeles. Several tracks had previously appeared on UK albums, singles, or EPs but were new to the American market, while others were unreleased tracks from earlier recording sessions. The album's title was proposed by the band's manager Andrew Loog Oldham, who attributed it in the liner notes to "Lou Folk-Rock Adler" as a facetious reference. Jagger described the title as Oldham's attempt at hip, Beat-style phrasing. The front cover photograph, taken by Gered Mankowitz, had previously been used for the UK edition of "Out of Our Heads". perplexity.description:
December’s Children (And Everybody’s) is the Rolling Stones’ fifth American studio album, issued by London Records in December 1965, and it captures the band in a transitional moment between their early R&B-heavy attack and the more ambitious songwriting that would soon define them. Compiled from U.S. and U.K. sources, it mixes recent singles, album tracks, EP material, and a few leftovers, giving it a patchwork feel that was typical of American Rolling Stones releases of the era.

Musically, the record ranges from raw blues rock and garagey rave-ups to sharper pop songwriting, with covers like “She Said Yeah” and “Route 66” sitting alongside the Jagger/Richards originals “Get Off of My Cloud” and “As Tears Go By.” Its significance lies in how clearly it documents the Stones’ evolution: the band were still rooted in American blues and R&B, but they were increasingly confident as writers and stylists, and the album has since been seen as a strong snapshot of their mid-1960s momentum.
